figures.finding: Fiji's Employment Relations Act 2007 sets the minimum age for employment at fifteen (s. 92) and lets children of thirteen to fifteen do light work, or work where family or communal or religious group members are employed, that does not harm their health or development or their attendance at school (s. 93); it sets no separate cap for light work, but no child (under eighteen, s. 4) may work more than 8 hours a day, with 30 minutes' paid rest in every 4 continuous hours (s. 97), and hazardous work is barred to children by ministerial order (s. 95). The DOL report first read held the light-work hours uncapped (lightWorkHoursCap null), which overlooked s. 97's cap on every child's day.
figures.applies: Fiji, the Act as consolidated on laws.gov.fj to 12 August 2026 (a reported amendment raising the age from 15 to 16 isn't in it).

sources.said: The age of 15 years is the minimum age for employment of children.

Subsection (1) does not apply to a child of 13 to 15 years of age engaged in employment or light work or in a workplace in which members of the same family or of communal or religious group are employed
child means a person who is under the age of 18 years
A child must— (a) not be employed or permitted to be employed for more than 8 hours in a day; and (b) be given at least 30 minutes paid rest for every continuous 4 hours worked.

figures.finding: Under Fiji's Companies Act 2015, s. 93(1), only a natural person of at least eighteen may be a director or secretary of a company, so a minor may hold shares in a producer's company but direct it only from eighteen.
figures.applies: Fiji, the Act as consolidated on laws.gov.fj to 12 August 2026.

sources.said: Only a natural person who is at least 18 years of age may be appointed as a director or secretary of a company.

sources.title: Employment Relations Act 2007, ss. 4, 92, 93, 95, 97 (Laws of Fiji, Office of the Solicitor-General, laws.gov.fj; consolidated to 12 August 2026; read through the site's own API, retrieve_html/LOF.CAP92.ERAFJ07.S<n>)
sources.said: [EMP 92] Minimum age for employment The age of 15 years is the minimum age for employment of children. [EMP 93] Employment of children under 15 years (1) A child under the age of 15 years must not be employed in any capacity other than in accordance with subsection (2) ... (2) Subsection (1) does not apply to a child of 13 to 15 years of age engaged in employment or light work or in a workplace in which members of the same family or of communal or religious group are employed provided that— (a) the employment is not likely to be harmful to the health or development of the child; and (b) the employment is not such as to prejudice the child’s attendance at school ... [s. 4] child means a person who is under the age of 18 years ... [EMP 95] (2) The Minister may ... by order in the Gazette, declare any employment or workplace to be a prohibited or restricted employment or workplace for the purposes of this Part on the ground that it is injurious to health or is hazardous ... [EMP 97] (1) A child must— (a) not be employed or permitted to be employed for more than 8 hours in a day; and (b) be given at least 30 minutes paid rest for every continuous 4 hours worked.

sources.title: Companies Act 2015, s. 93 (Laws of Fiji, laws.gov.fj; consolidated to 12 August 2026)
sources.said: [COM 93] Who can be a director (1) Only a natural person who is at least 18 years of age may be appointed as a director or secretary of a company.
